newsitem.title: UK: PCs to drive Dixons' profit power-surge.
newsitem.headline: PCs to drive Dixons' profit power-surge.

text.p: Britain's leading electricals retailer Dixons Group Plc, is set to reap annual profits surge 40 percent when it reports results next Wednesday.

The strong consumer demand and weaker competition is predicted to boost pre-exceptional profits to between 180 and 196.5 million stg in the year to end April from 135.2 million a year ago. Analysts see the dividend increasing to between 10 and 10.8 pence a share, from 8.75.
The group has enjoyed strong sales as a result of a personal computers boom as well as a general revival in consumer spending.

Dixons has been rapidly expanding its out-of-town PC World chain to capitalise on shoppers' appetite for hi-tech goods. Sales are still growing strongly, but the pace has been slackening, analysts said.

PC World saw total sales soar 96 percent in the first half, or by 21 percent stripping out new selling space. PCs and accessories, including software made up about 26 percent of the group's total sales in the first half. Dixons' other stores are Dixons in town centres and Currys out-of-town outlets selling larger electrical goods.
Analysts expected the second half could show slower growth, but the sales figures will be up against very strong increases in the second half of last year.
The electricals market has softened in the second half, which may have affected Dixons performance, analysts said.
"The overall market for durables has been slower in the second half," said one retail analyst, "particularly for audio equipment and small electricals," he said.
The group's shares have fallen under a cloud recently due to uncertainty about the impact of a Monopolies and Mergers Commission report into recommended prices for electrical goods.
Expectations that the MMC will recommend the scrapping of recommended prices hit Dixons shares in May, but analysts now believe small independent retailers will suffer most if the prices are banned.
The shares also took a beating after Chairman Sir Stanley Kalms sold 1.1 million of his holding back in February.
They were 1-1/2 pence down at 482-1/2 by 0745 GMT on Friday in a falling .
